$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}=\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}$

We can calculate the change in $x$ and change in $y$ by picking any two pairs of corresponding $x$- and $y$-values.

$\begin{array}{lrrrr}
&&\xrightarrow{+4}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+4}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+4}\,\,\,\,
\\
x
&45
&49
&53
&57
\\
\hline
\\
y
&10
&5
&0
&-5
\\
&&\xrightarrow[-5]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[-5]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[-5]{}\,\,\,\,
\end{array}$

So the slope is:

$\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}=\dfrac{-5}{4}=-\dfrac54$
